topics.topic: Owner-session identity collision handling during sign-in
questions: While holding the table lock, must sign-in check that the newly minted session identity is absent and mint again on collision, or may insertion overwrite or refuse?
What must sign-in do if the newly generated owner-session identity already names an entry in the session table?

quotes:
Substitution: two sign-ins are two sessions, each ending on its own; a CSRF
protection is bound to one (R0-29). Continuity: the same session carries the
owner's actions from sign-in until it ends.

During a lockout every sign-in is refused, the right credential included,
and is not counted; the lockout is not extended; the credential is compared
through `random_values.equal_in_constant_time`; one answer whatever was
wrong, never echoing it; concurrent sign-ins counted one at a time; other
open sessions stay (A13 rules 2–4). The identity and the CSRF value come
from `random_values.make_secret_value`.

A new owner session (M11) with its sign-in reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading`, no pending confirmation and no uploaded file; the
refusal count cleared. A refused sign-in outside a lockout counts at its
reading; the fifth less than 15 minutes old starts a 15-minute lockout.
judgement.why: A successful sign-in must create a distinct session while every existing session stays, so a colliding generated identity cannot overwrite, alias, or cause an additional refusal and must be replaced with a distinct value.

topics.topic: Concurrent traversal semantics for the owner-session table
questions: How do operations that must visit multiple or all sessions—especially the expiry pass and `drop_uploaded_files` after an import—enumerate the table, and what happens when entries are added or removed during that traversal?

quotes:
### Outputs

That every upload is dropped.

### Observable effect

No session keeps an uploaded file.

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing.

The session ends; its pending confirmation and its uploaded file are
dropped (M11).
judgement.why: The traversal mechanism is internal, while the required observable results are fixed: sign-out drops the removed session's upload, bulk cleanup leaves no upload in any session and cannot fail, and the expiry pass decides every session from one reading in sign-in order.

topics.topic: Locking and validity checks required when returning a session CSRF secret
questions: Does `give_session_csrf` merely return the value found by table lookup, or must it also take the session lock and recheck validity and ended state before returning the secret?

quotes:
The identity is looked up as the session check
looks it up, compared in constant time, under the session table's lock that
a sign-out, the pass and a sign-in take to end or make a session, so it
answers the value or none as the session stands before or after such an
end, never in between. It is asked after the request was
admitted, so a session that reached a limit while the request ran still
answers its value, and the page of a request that passed completes (A13
rule 2); a session ended since answers none, and the page is rendered
without forms that need one.
judgement.why: The operation performs the lookup under the table lock after admission, returns the value for a still-present session even if its limit was reached during the admitted request, and returns none if the session has since ended.

topics.topic: Request arrival ordering across table lookup and session-lock acquisition
questions: How does a request reserve its arrival-time check and its place on the session lock when it must first look the session up under a separately contended table lock?

quotes:
Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading` this operation takes when it is called, which for
an upload is after its bounded head has been read (A13 rule 2): a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5). A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2).

`admit_owner_request` reads `clock.monotonic_reading` when it is called and
  checks the session there; an upload arrives once its bounded head has
  been read. Nothing is held between a request's headers and its admission.
judgement.why: Arrival is the call to admit_owner_request and its monotonic reading, and a request valid at that reading must complete despite later waiting, expiry, or sign-out.

topics.topic: Session-entry lifetime after releasing the table lock
questions: After the table lock is released, what keeps the looked-up session entry valid if sign-out or the expiry pass removes it before the caller finishes using it?

quotes:
A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2). After the check, a change that touches no uploaded file takes its
place on the session's lock at once; a request that touches one first waits
for the import lock and then takes its place, so the locks are always taken
import first and no place on a session's lock waits for the import lock (A16
rule 2).

Its turn on the session's lock comes after every change of the session
admitted before it: one touching no uploaded file took its place at its
admission, before the sign-out, which takes its own only after the import
lock; one touching an uploaded file asked for the import lock before the
sign-out did, and that lock is granted in order (`admit_owner_request`).
Each completes first, its change to the store
included, with the confirmation and the upload it may need still in place,
and leaves nothing in the ended session.
judgement.why: Admission reserves the request's completion and lock position, so a later sign-out cannot invalidate its session reference or make the already-admitted request recheck and refuse.

topics.topic: Whether lock ordering constrains only nested locks or also sequential acquisition
questions: Is this order a nesting order only for locks held simultaneously, or does it forbid acquiring a session lock after a completed table-lock lookup?

quotes:
It is taken last — after the import lock,
  the sign-in lock and a session's lock, where the path holds them — and
  released before any other lock is taken, so the order of all four is
  import, sign-in, session, table, and no holder of the table lock waits for
  another (owner, 2026-11-17).
judgement.why: The qualification “where the path holds them” makes the order a co-held-lock order, and the explicit release-before-another-lock rule permits releasing the table lock and then acquiring a session lock.
